about: The template for the stage 4 public deployment: the stage 4 system, as stage-4-local.json describes it, deployed once to Arbitrum Sepolia (D-14) by demo/public-run stage-4 and left running by demo/public-run serve. Nothing is deployed yet: every address is null until a run fills it. The run reads the node, model, price, signer limits, LPT, pool, faucet and parameter change values below, so what runs is what this file says, and writes its own copy, with the chain id, the addresses, the source commit, the accounts and what the standing services need, to its state directory. That copy, once a run on Arbitrum Sepolia has reconciled, is the manifest to keep here. The stage 3 template, public-arbitrum-sepolia.json, still runs with demo/public-run.

contracts.checks: only the executor Parameters' group 10 names for the round a draw runs in may draw the network share (drawNetwork); at deployment that is the Buyback

contracts.node_name: none: Parameters names it as the deployment's score source, and Claims reads it as its validator set

none: the Broker reads its fee split from it, Claims, StakeLedger and Scores their values, and the Buyback its values (S-07's view, groups 8 and 9), and the Broker the executor that may draw (group 10)
contracts.checks: authority() is G, the authority key the owner gives the run; deployed after the TestPool, at the address the Broker, StakeLedger and Scores were given; its deployment buyback values are the TestPool and the buyback values below, and its deployment executor (group 10) is the Buyback, taken at construction as the address predicted for it
broker() is the Broker, values() is Parameters, poolCodeHash() is the runtime code hash of the TestPool deployed with it, and acceptsPool(TestPool) is true

node.changes: none: the unmodified node, configured by flags alone

chain.kind: Arbitrum Sepolia, a public test chain (D-14)
chain.round_clock: block.number, which on Arbitrum is close to the L1 block number (about one every 12 s), and the node's clock is the header's l1BlockNumber: one round of 50 blocks is about 10 minutes. Round 1 starts with the clock's deployment; the parameter change, announced in round 1, counts from round 8, about 70 minutes later, and the first buy comes once the pool's average price is an interval old (3,600 s, about six rounds) and the network share holds the job's half

price.ticket_face: the job price in micro-USDC plus 1: one ticket of 1 USDC a job

pool.note: Seeded by the deployer from its genesis LPT and freshly minted mock USDC: 5.000000 USDC per LPT (S-07 section 1)

faucet.note: 1,000,000 test LPT of the genesis supply, granted at deployment to the faucet account the run makes, so that test LPT can be handed out later without the deployer's key. Nothing hands it out yet

parameter_change.name: unbonding
parameter_change.note: The change the run announces as G right after the deployment and reads back in the round before it counts and in the round it counts from: the unbonding period, 21 rounds at deployment, to 42, inside D-47's range of 1 to 840. Nothing in the run unbonds, so no figure of the run depends on it

stand_ins.stand_in: Role accounts made by the run
stand_ins.for: Operators who hold their own keys
stand_ins.value: The deployer's and the authority's keys are the owner's, each given by a keystore path outside the repository. The node N, the payer P, the validator V, the keeper and the faucet are keys the run makes and keeps only in its state directory, each paid its gas money by the deployer at the start; the standing services use these and never the deployer's

An ERC-20 with six decimals that anyone may mint (contracts/src/money/MockUSDC.sol). On a public chain anyone can mint it, so the run's figure of all USDC in existence holds only while nobody outside the run has minted any; the run says so when it differs
The node prices in wei of the chain's native token. With 1,000,000 of its units to the dollar, one unit is one micro-USDC, so 1 USDC = 1 USD and the node's amounts are micro-USDC

Win probability 2^256 - 2, the largest the node accepts, and a face of the job price + 1 micro-USDC (0.999999 USD = 999,999, so 1,000,000: one ticket of 1 USDC a job). Each job settles one ticket and overpays 1 micro-USDC (D-06)

stand_ins.stand_in: The signer's ticket limits in micro-USDC
stand_ins.value: --max-ticket-ev 2000000 and --max-batch-ev 20000000, read as micro-USDC because of the fixed rate above
RoundLength = 50 blocks of the block number the node reads (R-18): on Arbitrum the L1 block number, so about 10 minutes a round; a round lasts longer when nobody starts the next one
SmolLM2-135M-Instruct served by llama.cpp; its answers are not checked, and a settled ticket does not show the work was done

stand_ins.for: Governance announcing parameter changes under D-12 (S-10 R-25)
stand_ins.value: A key the owner makes for the testnet alone and gives the run as a keystore outside the repository, fixed in Parameters at deployment as its one authority: it announces and withdraws with lp2-params, and a change counts from the announce round + 7. No contract has an owner key, and the Controller's names are fixed at deployment

stand_ins.for: A Uniswap v2 pool of USDC and LPT on a public chain
stand_ins.value: A port of the v2 pair's mint and swap paths with v2's fee, cumulative prices and revert texts, no owner, no protocol fee and no flash swaps (contracts/src/money/TestPool.sol), seeded by the deployer at deployment with 500,000 mock USDC and 100,000 test LPT; the Buyback admits only a pool with its runtime code hash and this deployment's two tokens

Parameters holds burn 100 %, TWAP interval 3,600 s, slippage bound 1 %, a buy every round and the TestPool above until G announces a change; the burn share is fixed (D-47 (v)). The executor, group 10, is the Buyback until G announces another; a later executor and pool are named by announcement, with nothing else redeployed

stand_ins.for: A network share made by real traffic
stand_ins.value: The network share the first buy spends is the half of the one job N serves in round 2, 0.5 test USDC. The pool and the slippage bound would allow a buy of about 3,495 USDC

stand_ins.for: The way people outside the team get test LPT to bond
stand_ins.value: A key the run makes, granted the faucet share of genesis test LPT above at deployment; nothing hands it out yet
An ERC-20 with 18 decimals (contracts/src/money/TestLPT.sol) that only Claims, fixed at deployment, may mint
Created once by the token's constructor for the deployer, outside every round's issuance (R-09); holders are given LPT from it by transfer (the ledger case's grant_lpt), never by a mint
An address the run makes up and whose key nobody holds, fixed in Claims at deployment; it receives each round's treasury amount and what the validator division leaves

One validator, V, a registered node with 1,000 test LPT of its own, run by programs/validators: in the run from demo/public-validators.script, which opts it in in round 2, so that it is the only member from round 3, and casts no vote; under demo/public-run serve from a script the services write, in which V votes the full score, 1,000,000, for N in the round after they start, which leaves every score as it was. The S-06 division of each round's validator amount is paid to it
Scores seats at most 3 members, Parameters' validator set size at deployment, which G may change (R-25); the public run seats one

stand_ins.for: Whoever starts rounds, mints each round's validator and treasury amounts, buys and pokes
stand_ins.value: lp2-keeper with a key the run makes, given Parameters' address: it buys or pokes at the executor in force for the round only when its call would succeed. The run starts it, and demo/public-run serve keeps it running after the run. Anyone may do any of these (R-10, R-16, R-18), so a stopped keeper delays them and loses nothing
